source: second occurrence: user evaluated @heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty after pi-claude-style-tools already broke `pi` startup via read-tool conflict with pi-hashline-edit-pro
summary: REINFORCED PATTERN (now 2 instances): Pi tool-output RENDERER extensions re-register built-in tool names to restyle them, which hard-conflicts with pi-hashline-edit-pro (owns `read`+`replace`). pi-claude-style-tools registered `read` -> `pi` refused to start ('Tool "read" conflicts'). @heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-pretty (MIT v0.4.4) does the SAME: source `pi.registerTool({...origRead, name:"read"})` plus bash/ls/find/grep/multi_grep, and bundles @ff-labs/fff-node owning find/grep. source: design analysis 2026-07-05 (medivance session relayed a 'skip superseded rows' proposal; refined here) - PENDING user option-gate decision, not yet approved
summary: Design decision (open gate): should graph-hygiene skip retired history for missing-path / migration proposals? KEY SEMANTIC distinction surfaced: missing-path on an ACTIVE row = genuinely missing, actionable (add the record/fix the path); missing-path on a RETIRED (superseded) row = intentionally-removed history (e.g. ADR-0050-deleted jcode-wiring.ts) that must NOT be re-created. Correct fix = Option A 'retired id-GROUP skip': if any row in an id-group has status:superseded, treat the whole group (including the still-active original that append-only never modified) as retired and exclude it from missing-path/comma/removed-ref/legacy-proposal - but KEEP active-row missing-paths visible. medivance session's literal 'skip superseded rows' (Option B) is incomplete under append-only because the original row stays active/unstatused. Implementation would be a two-pass in graph-hygiene.ts inspect() (pass 1 build id->hasSuperseded, pass 2 apply), + graph-hygiene SDD + progressive-knowledge-graph SDD + self-test. | UPDATE 2026-07-05: a medivance host session running lazy-graph-migrate correctly STOPPED (reason-based skill worked) and surfaced a host-side user-confirmed decision (medivance planning graph-hygiene-migration-detector-conflict.md, 'Option A — framework detector 확장이 fix; host graph untouched; do NOT bulk-append 95 supersede rows — noise, no count benefit; removed-16 already in-place superseded; record-body-jcode-99 out of scope'). This ALIGNS with this candidate: the fix is a FRAMEWORK graph-hygiene.ts detector change (status/meaning-aware: skip retired/superseded groups for missing-path/removed-ref, and do NOT flag legacy rows that already carry a meaningful type-predicate as needing conversion — they are KEEP), so hosts get clean counts via lazy update WITHOUT churning host graphs. Measured medivance: 968 rows, 21 missing-path warnings, 95 legacy(raw), 16 removed(already superseded in-place), 99 record-jcode. Pending user go-ahead to implement the detector extension in lazy-harness.
resolution: Implemented 2026-07-05 (user-approved Option A): graph-hygiene.ts retired-id-group skip (two-pass) - id-group with any status:superseded row is retired; skip missing-path/comma/legacy/removed-ref for retired rows, ACTIVE still flagged; read-only, host graph untouched. graph-hygiene SDD Must + self-test graph4 fixture; framework host-name leak removed. Framework graph legacy 42->37, active missing-paths preserved.

source: diagnosis 2026-07-05 while answering how a downstream host with residual graph counts should proceed (read-only graph-hygiene --migration-plan inspection)
summary: Generalizable host-graph pattern (host-agnostic): early-seeded host graphs can carry ACTIVE (no status) rows that assert facts about framework capabilities later REMOVED by ADR 0050 (e.g. references to jcode-wiring.ts, task-router.ts, context-index/delivery/broker, graph-explain.md). After the retired-id-group skip landed, these still surface (correctly) as removed-framework-ref + missing-path because they are ACTIVE, not superseded. Reason-based verdict distinction: these are SUPERSEDE candidates (the FACT is genuinely obsolete — the capability was removed for a real reason, ADR 0050), NOT legacy-shape KEEP (contrast: a host whose residual rows were already superseded/legacy-shape needs no churn and clears via lazy update alone). Prescription: the host runs ONE reason-based lazy-graph-migrate pass in ITS OWN session (host-owned, root-bound) — SUPERSEDE the framework-obsolete active rows citing ADR 0050, and per-case judge any host-specific missing-paths (fix/add vs supersede). This is legitimate reasoned supersession, not noise-churn. Consider adding this case to the host conversion runbook. Example measured (one host): 23 removed-ref + 49 missing-path (~40 framework-internal + ~9 host-specific).
